help.intro: Five prepositions always take the accusative, whatever the sentence: durch (through), für (for), gegen (against), ohne (without), um (around; at a time). After them the article shifts to its accusative form — which, as ever, only shows on the masculine: für den Mann, durch den Park, ohne den Schlüssel; feminine and neuter look unchanged: für die Frau, für das Kind. This is the first time a preposition, rather than a verb, decides the case — a pattern that will grow later in the course (dative prepositions, then the two-way ones). Learn these five as a chant; there are no exceptions. Most items ask for the article; five ask for the preposition itself, from its English meaning.
help.tips[0].text: Five beats. Say it, clap it, walk to it. These five are always accusative, no exceptions, no thinking.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: through the park, for the man, against the wall, without the car, around the table
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: The bus drives through the village.
help.tips[0].check.q: Which preposition always takes the accusative?
help.tips[0].check.why: ohne is one of the five: durch, für, gegen, ohne, um. mit and aus take a different case.
help.tips[1].title: What actually changes
help.tips[1].text: Only the masculine: der → den, ein → einen, mein → meinen. für die Mutter and für das Kind look like the nominative.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: The present is for the father. The flowers are for the mother.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: Without the key I can't get in.
help.tips[1].trap: English 'for the' never changes. In German the preposition reaches over and bends the article.
help.tips[1].check.q: Ich kaufe Blumen für ____ Freund. (der Freund)
help.tips[1].check.why: für takes the accusative, and Freund is masculine, so mein becomes meinen.
help.tips[2].title: Contractions you will hear
help.tips[2].text: für das → fürs, durch das → durchs, um das → ums. Casual, common, correct: fürs Kind, ums Haus.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: The present is for the child.
help.tips[2].check.why: für + das melts into fürs. für alone is missing the article, and den is wrong for a das-word.
help.tips[3].title: um is also "at" for times
help.tips[3].text: um acht Uhr (at eight). Same preposition, no article needed. Don't confuse it with the movement sense: um den See, um den Tisch.
help.tips[3].examples[0].en: At seven we run around the lake.
help.tips[3].check.why: For a clock time German uses um: um acht Uhr, with no article.
help.remember[1]: The article after them: den for blue words, otherwise unchanged.
help.context.en: I'm buying a present for my brother. We walk through the park and then around the lake. He never goes for a walk without the dog. Around six we're back – hopefully without rain!
help.mistakes[0].why: für takes the accusative: der → den.
help.mistakes[1].why: Possessives take the ein-ending: meinen for a masculine object.
help.hook: Learn five little words (durch, für, gegen, ohne, um) and you'll know exactly which article follows them, every time.

sentences[0].explanationSections[0]: für, durch, gegen, ohne, um always take the accusative. der → den, die → die, das → das.
sentences[0].why: für always takes the accusative: der Mann → den Mann.
sentences[1].english: I buy something for the mother.
sentences[1].why: für + accusative; die-words don't change there: die Mutter.
sentences[2].english: That is a gift for the child.
sentences[2].why: für + accusative; das-words stay das: für das Kind.
sentences[3].why: durch always takes the accusative: der Park → den Park.
sentences[4].why: 'Through' is durch — one of the five always-accusative prepositions (durch, für, gegen, ohne, um).
sentences[5].english: I have nothing against the plan.
sentences[5].why: gegen takes the accusative: der Plan → den Plan.
sentences[6].english: Without the car it is hard.
sentences[6].why: 'Without' is ohne — always with the accusative.
sentences[7].why: ohne + accusative; die Tasche keeps die.
sentences[8].why: um ('around') takes the accusative: der Tisch → den Tisch.
sentences[9].english: The car drives into the tree.
sentences[9].why: 'Against / into' is gegen — den Baum shows its accusative.
sentences[10].english: The bus drives through the village.
sentences[10].why: durch + accusative; das-words don't change: durch das Dorf.
sentences[11].english: The flowers are for the woman.
sentences[11].why: 'For' is für — always accusative, which die Frau doesn't show.
sentences[12].why: gegen + accusative; die Mannschaft stays die.
sentences[13].english: Without the key I cannot get in.
sentences[13].why: ohne + accusative: der Schlüssel → den Schlüssel.
sentences[14].why: 'Around' is um — den See is its accusative.
sentences[15].english: I'm buying a cake for the neighbour.
sentences[15].why: für + accusative: den — and Nachbar even adds -n itself (a weak noun).
sentences[16].english: We're going on holiday without the dog.
sentences[16].why: ohne + accusative: der Hund → den Hund.
sentences[17].english: The children run around the tree.
sentences[17].why: um + accusative: der Baum → den Baum.
sentences[18].english: I'm against the idea. It isn't good.
sentences[18].why: 'Against' an idea is gegen — gegen die Idee, accusative as always.
